title: Persist Heatmap show-labels toggle to session widgets
observed_behavior: The Show Labels toggle updated the rendered Heatmap but did not persist heatmap-axislabels-show in session widgets, so widget-backed state and the reopened dialog could drift from the current Plotly label visibility.
intended_behavior: Toggling Show Labels should update the heatmap-axislabels-show widget so the persisted Heatmap state and rendered Plotly axis-label visibility stay aligned.
cause_summary: The template bound ngModel directly to heatmapShowLabels and only called redrawHeatmap(), which never wrote the new value back into session.style.widgets.
fix_summary: Added updateShowLabels() to persist heatmap-axislabels-show before redrawing, and the maintained Heatmap controls journey now asserts the widget and Plotly label visibility together.
notes: Found while wiring maintained Heatmap settings coverage.

title: Guard Heatmap export for missing gradient overlay data
observed_behavior: Exporting the Heatmap image could throw before writing the file when fixGradient() assumed a .gradient_filled element always existed in the rendered Plotly content.
intended_behavior: Heatmap export should succeed for Plotly heatmaps even when the rendered content does not include a gradient_filled element.
cause_summary: fixGradient() dereferenced insertionPoint[0] and its fill style unconditionally, but Heatmap exports do not always render a gradient_filled node or a fragment-based fill value.
fix_summary: Guarded fixGradient() for the no-gradient and no-fragment-id cases so SVG export can complete on the maintained Heatmap fixture.
notes: Found while adding the Heatmap export regression test.

title: Align Heatmap distance-matrix export with rendered axes order
observed_behavior: Exporting the Heatmap distance matrix could disagree with the rendered Heatmap when axes were inverted because the CSV serialization kept the base getDM() ordering instead of the active Plotly ordering.
intended_behavior: Heatmap CSV export should reflect the currently rendered Heatmap orientation for invertX invertY and label visibility.
cause_summary: saveDistanceMatrix() built the CSV from the raw getDM() matrix and only partially reused Heatmap labels, so the exported rows and columns could drift from the rendered Plotly trace under active inversion.
fix_summary: Updated saveDistanceMatrix() to clone the backing matrix apply active invertX and invertY before serialization and save a real CSV blob, and the maintained controls journey now compares the exported CSV payload directly to the rendered Heatmap trace in both labeled and unlabeled states.
notes: Found while adding maintained Heatmap CSV export coverage.

title: Refresh active Heatmap when distance metric changes
observed_behavior: Changing the default distance metric while Heatmap was already active could leave the view showing the old metric label and matrix until the user manually reopened or redrew the tab.
intended_behavior: An already-active Heatmap should redraw when underlying network data changes including post-launch metric switches on sequence-derived datasets.
cause_summary: The Heatmap component did not participate in the networkUpdated redraw flow and lacked an updateVisualization() hook, so recomputed sequence-derived distances did not rerender the active Plotly heatmap.
fix_summary: Added a networkUpdated subscription redraw on tab show and an updateVisualization() implementation so active Heatmap tabs refresh when network state changes, and the maintained metric-switch journey now asserts the recomputed Heatmap state on both FASTA and sequence-node-list inputs.
notes: Found while adding maintained post-launch Heatmap metric-switch coverage.

title: Expose Heatmap as a direct-launch view option
observed_behavior: The File Settings View to Launch control did not offer Heatmap as an option, so uploaded datasets could not open directly into Heatmap even though the app already supported the Heatmap view.
intended_behavior: Heatmap should be selectable as a launch target anywhere the product supports Heatmap as a first-class view.
cause_summary: The File Settings default-view select omitted a Heatmap option, which blocked the launch widget from ever setting default-view to Heatmap through the UI.
fix_summary: Added Heatmap to the File Settings launch-view select and covered the direct-launch path with a maintained uploaded-data matrix across all Heatmap-capable fixtures.
notes: Found while closing the remaining Heatmap direct-launch gap.

title: Refresh Heatmap styling when global background changes
observed_behavior: Changing the global background color while Heatmap was active updated the 2D canvas widget state but left the active Heatmap background and axis text unchanged until a manual redraw, and background-color-contrast was not recomputed from the new background.
intended_behavior: Global background changes should immediately restyle an active Heatmap and keep axis text contrast aligned with the chosen background color.
cause_summary: onBackgroundChanged() only wrote background-color and updated #cy, so Plotly-based Heatmap never received a visualization refresh and the contrast widget stayed stale.
fix_summary: Updated onBackgroundChanged() to recompute background-color-contrast with contrastColor(), persist both widgets, and publish visualization updates so active Heatmap tabs restyle in place; the maintained background regression now asserts the rendered Plotly background and axis-text colors.
notes: Found while closing the final Heatmap styling gap.

title: Mark Heatmap rendered when direct-launch drawing completes
observed_behavior: Launching directly into Heatmap could leave the Processing Files modal open even after the Plotly heatmap rendered, which blocked the completed app state and made direct-launch readiness appear hung.
intended_behavior: A Heatmap-first launch should mark the network as rendered once the Plotly view finishes drawing so the loading modal clears and post-launch flows can continue.
cause_summary: The Heatmap component rendered with Plotly but never called setNetworkRendered(true), so the launch workflow did not receive the completion signal used by other first-class views.
fix_summary: Updated drawHeatmap() to set the background and then mark networkRendered after the Plotly render promise resolves, allowing direct Heatmap launches to complete cleanly across uploaded file types.
notes: Found while validating the maintained Heatmap direct-launch matrix.
